title: Sparse Frame Handshake for Unstable Networks (PRD sketch)
content:
Context and motivation:

We get recurrent asks from customers building on mobile and edge platforms: intermittent connectivity, tight upload budgets, and long tail packet loss make full streaming contracts brittle. Mobile SDKs often need a tiny, explicit handshake that negotiates how much structure and fidelity the client will accept, how tool-calls are surfaced incrementally, and what the server will fall back to when packets drop or connections re-establish.

This doc sketches a "Sparse Frame Handshake" PRD: a minimal, negotiated frame protocol for hosted streaming that prioritizes predictable latency and graceful fidelity degradation while preserving tooling semantics (tool calls, structured JSON outputs). Goal is to propose an SDK-facing surface, wire semantics, server behavior, and a rollout plan for experiments.

Problem statements (user-centric):
- Mobile product engineers: "When the device is on flaky LTE, I can't rely on long JSON blobs or large streaming frames; app UX hangs or duplicates tool calls after reconnects."
- Platform SDK maintainers: "We need a simple surface that app developers can adopt quickly, with safe fallbacks and clear telemetry."
- Platform reliability/product teams: "We must avoid inconsistent side effects from repeated tool invocation during reconnects; e.g., duplicate webhooks or DB writes."

Primary objectives (measurable):
- Reduce perceived median time-to-first-meaningful-token for mobile clients by 25% in low-bandwidth >90th percentile scenarios (measured via synthetic LTE tests).
- Decrease duplicate tool invocations due to reconnects by 90% for clients using the handshake and idempotency tokens.
- Provide a client-side API that is <= 4 surface calls to get streaming + tool-calls running (simplicity).

Constraints and non-goals:
- Not trying to replace full streaming contracts for desktop/web. This is targeted at unstable/mobile networks and small payloads.
- Not a security design doc; assume existing auth/KMS flows remain.
- We will not change server-side model semantics; only the streaming transport and client handshake.

High-level design summary:
1) Handshake phase (single small request/response) negotiated at session start. Client indicates network posture, max frame size, and desired fidelity level. Server responds with the supported minimal schema and session id.
2) Sparse frames: Each incremental piece of output is encoded in a tiny, stable frame schema (see examples). Frames are intentionally compact (short keys, optional fields omitted) and idempotency-aware.
3) Progressive fidelity levels: 0..3 (0 = metadata-only, 1 = sketch/intent, 2 = partial structured output, 3 = full fidelity). The server may emit lower fidelity frames first and upgrade to higher fidelity when bandwidth allows.
4) Tool-call semantics: Tool invocations are emitted as dedicated frames with call-id, idempotency token, and coalescing hints. The client SDK guarantees single-execution semantics by acknowledging tool frames; server retries are gated by idempotency.
5) Reconnect/resume: Session ids + last-seen frame cursors allow resume without re-executing tool frames. If the server cannot guarantee idempotency (e.g., external side-effect occurred), it emits a "reconcile" frame instructing client how to present to user.

Detailed wire format (sketch):
- All frames are newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) over the existing streaming transport (HTTP/2 or websockets).
- Frame size target: <= 1–2 KB for most payloads by default.
- Keys are short: t (type), s (session), i (cursor id), c (content), m (meta), f (fidelity), T (tool), id (call id), tok (idempotency token).

Example frames: (note: these are intentionally terse)
- Handshake request (client): {"t":"hs_req","m":{"net":"flaky","upl_bandwidth_kbps":200},"f":1}\n
- Handshake response (server): {"t":"hs_res","s":"sess_3e7","f":1,"m":{"schema":"sparse-v1","keepalive":15}}\n
- Partial content frame (sketch): {"t":"out","s":"sess_3e7","i":12,"f":1,"c":"todo: outline flow for user"}\n
- Tool-call frame: {"t":"tool","s":"sess_3e7","T":"search","id":"call_45","tok":"abc123","m":{"hint":"coalesce"}}\n
- Tool-ack frame (client->server): {"t":"ack","s":"sess_3e7","id":"call_45","status":"ok"}\n
- Upgrade to structured partial frame: {"t":"out","s":"sess_3e7","i":14,"f":2,"c":{"summary":"3 steps","items":["a","b"]}}\n
- Reconcile frame (server): {"t":"recon","s":"sess_3e7","id":"call_45","m":{"reason":"external_side_effect","action":"present_conflict"}}\n
Server behavior rules (important for safety):
- On emitting a tool frame, server records id + tokens in durable session state. A tool frame is not considered "final" until acknowledged or until server policy timeout.
- If connection breaks before ack: server retains call state for X seconds (configurable per-tier) and will either retry (if safe) or emit reconcile to new session.
- For non-idempotent tools, server will prefer to emit preview frames describing the intended side-effect and wait for explicit client confirmation before executing.

SDK ergonomics (mobile-first recommendations):
- Minimal developer surface: Session.start(handshakeOptions) -> returns session object with events: onFrame(fn), onToolCall(fn), onReconnect(fn).
- Automatic ack manager: SDK auto-acks simple tool calls unless developer opts into manual ack for high-safety flows.
- Reconciliation hooks: SDK exposes a simple promise API: session.reconcile(callId) -> shows UI or programmatic decision and returns user decision to server.
- Offline queueing: When offline, SDK will persist un-acked local acks only; it will avoid re-sending tool-call execution commands unless explicit.
- Size-aware telemetry: SDK exposes a telemetry flag to annotate per-frame size, round-trip time, and reconnect causes.

Developer UX examples (pseudocode):
- Quick path for chat with simple tools (pseudocode):
  const s = await Session.start({net:'flaky', fidelity:1});
  s.onFrame(f => renderText(f.c));
  s.onToolCall(t => { if (t.m.hint === 'coalesce') showInlineButton('Run', () => s.ack(t.id)) });

- Manual safe execution flow:
  s.onToolCall(t => { showConfirmUI().then(dec => s.reconcile(t.id, dec)) });

Telemetry and success metrics to collect (must instrument):
- handshake_success_rate, avg_handshake_latency, percent_frames_under_1KB, median_time_to_first_sketch, duplicate_tool_calls_by_session, reconnect_resume_success_rate, reconcile_frame_frequency.

Security and privacy notes:
- Frames still carry auth headers on initial transport; sessions inherit server-side identity. No secret leakage in terse keys; SDKs should avoid logging tok values.
- Reconcile frames may include minimal contextual information only — full side-effect payloads must be fetched via secure side-channel if needed.

Rollout plan and experiments:
- Phase 0 (internal): Implement server-side session state + sparse frame encoder; provide a test SDK stub for iOS and Android. Run synthetic unstable network tests (20% packet drop, 300–800ms jitter).
- Phase 1 (pilot customers): Opt-in via SDK flag for a small set of mobile customers building editors and search UIs. Collect telemetry and user-reported UX.
- Phase 2 (general availability): If duplicate_tool_calls < 10% and median TTFM improves by >20% in pilot, default to handshake enabled on mobile SDKs with opt-out.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How long should the server retain un-acked tool frames for the Dedicated tier vs hosted API? (TBD; propose 5m for hosted, 30m for dedicated?)
- Should frames be compressed binary (CBOR) for next iteration to reduce size further? Migration complexity vs immediate wins?
- Backward compatibility: How to interoperate with clients that do not speak sparse frames? Server should provide full streaming fallback but disabled by default for mobile handshake sessions.
- UX: how do we present a "reconcile" event in chat UIs without surprising users? Need UX patterns.

Risks:
- Mis-implemented ack/retain semantics could still lead to duplicate side-effects. Mitigation: require idempotency tokens and server-side durable logging for all tool calls in pilot.
- Increased server state per session (session retention) may impact memory — implement compact on-disk durable store for call ids.

Appendix: implementation notes and quick ticket map
- Server: lightweight session-store + frame encoder (ticket API-1245).\n- SDKs: iOS/Android JS shim, auto-ack manager, reconnect resume logic (ticket SDK-330, SDK-331).\n- Observability: new telemetry metrics + synthetic test harness (ticket OBS-88).\n
Notes to reviewers:
- This is a sketch focusing on pragmatic wins for mobile. Please comment on: (1) fidelity levels, (2) ack windows, (3) tool-call idempotency model.
- Slack thread for design discussion: #prod-hosted-streaming (see linked_artifacts).

Quick todo list (short-term):
- [Priya] prototype NDJSON encoder and server-side state table (1 week)
- [Samir] build iOS stub SDK with auto-ack (2 weeks)
- [Elena] define telemetry dashboards and synthetic test scenarios (1 week)
- [All] review idempotency and reconcile UX patterns (async)

End of PRD sketch.
